observed_result.criterion: Verdict criterion H2 (control connections opened AFTER the stop only): after ssh -O stop, (a) -O check fails, (b) a new client using the old ControlPath makes a new, rejected connection (rc 255) and a client that cannot authenticate is not admitted, and (c) the already-open session S1 continues. Fail: H2 refuted (any admission of a new client after stop, or S1 killed). Scope note (M00-review-g04): this criterion does not cover control connections the master accepted before the stop; those are G09-prelim-mux-preconnected-after-stop (verdict fail: still admitted), so a pass here does NOT show that -O stop stops admissions. H1 (whether certificate expiry alone stops new multiplexed sessions), the master's exit after its last session, and -O exit effects are recorded as findings; they do not by themselves pass or fail the recipe.
observed_result.summary: Observed on fixture ca1 (certificate valid_before = master start + 90 s, ControlPersist=10m, no tty). (1) Certificate expiry does not stop admissions: at valid_before+10 s a fresh login was refused (rc 255, 'Certificate invalid: expired'), but a new multiplexed session through the existing master was ADMITTED (rc 0, no new TCP connection, no new Accepted line), and so was a client with PubkeyAuthentication=no (rc 0) (H1, H1b). (2) ssh -O stop: rc 0 ('Stop listening request sent.'); control socket removed; the master kept running (retitled 'ssh: [stopped mux]'); -O check rc 255; a client connecting AFTER the stop with the old ControlPath opened a new TCP connection that sshd refused as expired (rc 255), and one with PubkeyAuthentication=no was not admitted (rc 255) (H2a, H2b, H2b2). This only shows that the stop closes the door to NEW control connections: control connections the master accepted before the stop were still granted sessions and forwards after it (G09-prelim-mux-preconnected-after-stop, verdict fail), so this run does NOT show that -O stop stops admissions. (3) The already-open session S1 continued: 9 heartbeats after stop, last 44 s after it, normal end (rc 0, S1-END) (H2c); with no other control connection open, the master exited within the 0.5 s poll after S1 ended despite ControlPersist=10m (H2d; with an idle pre-accepted control connection the stopped master stays up). (4) -O exit on a second master: master gone, open session S2 terminated (rc 255, 0 heartbeats after exit), socket removed, later client refused (rc 255) (H3); but the remote no-tty shell of S2 (bash pid 815 in the container) was still running 7 s and 20 s after -O exit, with new sleep children (H3b): closing the connection is not remote-process termination. Verdict pass against the H2 criterion, which is scoped to new control connections. Consequence: owned masters must be CLOSED at the deadline (-O exit or exact-PID termination); -O stop is not a verified admission-stopping control (spec 6.6), and neither expiry nor closure ends remote processes.

limitations: OpenSSH mechanism evidence only: host client /usr/bin/ssh (OpenSSH_10.3p1, LibreSSL 3.3.6, macOS) against sshd (OpenSSH_10.0p2 Debian-7+deb13u4, OpenSSL 3.5.6 7 Apr 2026) in disposable Docker fixture containers. No Heimdall code exists or ran; this is not evidence of Heimdall behavior.

Not desktop-lock, sleep, logout, reboot or secure-store evidence: the dedicated agents are plain ssh-agent processes in an unlocked session started by the harness. Lock continuity remains open (owner-run probes).
Single machine: macOS 27.0 arm64 with Docker Desktop (linux VM). No native Windows/WSL or Linux-host evidence. The openssh-server package version is observed, not pinned (apt floats at image build).
Fixture sshd sets PerSourcePenalties no, unlike the OpenSSH 10 default.
Requirement IDs are listed for traceability; this record is not by itself evidence that any product requirement is met (tests/evidence/README.md).

Independent review M00-review-g04 (tests/evidence/artifacts/m00-wf2/review-g04.json) re-ran the earlier version of these experiments from scratch and refuted the earlier '-O stop: admissions stopped' conclusion; this record comes from the corrected harness (task M00-T04-G04-fix). The corrections themselves have not been independently re-reviewed.
One client/server version pair; masters started with -N -f and ControlPersist=10m; sessions without a tty; only Heimdall-like owned masters, no unmanaged connections.
Detached remote processes (nohup/setsid) were not tested; the remote-process listing only shows which processes of the account remained after -O exit.
Preliminary G09 evidence only: it does not select the ordinary/strict policy (spec P06) and does not cover clock skew, sleep across the deadline, or revocation.

H2 exercises only clients that connect to the control path after -O stop. A control connection accepted before the stop was still granted sessions and forwards after it (G09-prelim-mux-preconnected-after-stop). H2d (master exits after its last session) held because no other control connection was open in this run; with an idle pre-accepted control connection the stopped master stays up.
